How all-link telemetry is recorded

Method, as implemented in link_map.py and the controller's port-stats handler

The legacy telemetry recorded only the links out of s1, so the rest of the topology was invisible to the forecaster and to any graph model. link_map.py defines the port-to-link map as data: on every port-stats reply the controller resolves each switch port to its link (reported by the smaller endpoint switch, so each link is counted once) and writes one row per core link to telemetry_all_links.csv — utilization in percent as recorded, throughput, delay when measured, packet loss and active flows.

Utilization bands on this page use the controller's own congestion threshold: samples at or above 85% are the high band, 50–85% mid, above 0 and below 50% low, and exactly 0 idle. Peak time is the timestamp of the link's maximum recorded sample, read from the rows themselves.

This file is also the training substrate for the graph forecaster: experiments/pool_telemetry.py pools these captures into one timeline the GNN's link line-graph is built from. For the paper, this page is the reproducibility surface for the data-coverage claim — every aggregate is recomputed at request time from the recorded files named in the source list.
